summary: Harvard's free, open textbook and curriculum on machine learning systems, with hands-on labs, kits and TinyTorch, a framework you build yourself.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Machine Learning Systems is an open curriculum from Harvard for learning AI engineering. It centres on a textbook series, with Volume I (Introduction to Machine Learning Systems) released and forthcoming in print from MIT Press, and later volumes on scaling, agentic systems and physical AI. The repository also holds TinyTorch, the MLSys·im modeling tool, hardware kits, labs, slides, study sheets and an instructor hub.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most ML courses teach models, not the systems that run them. This curriculum connects ML ideas to how they execute efficiently on real hardware, at scale and in production.
whoFor: Students and self-learners in AI engineering
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, structured path that pairs reading with building, from a textbook to writing your own mini framework.
requirements: A web browser to read online
For TinyTorch and labs, see each component's own guide

overview: Students start by reading Volume I at mlsysbook.ai, then build TinyTorch, model systems with MLSys·im, review chapters with study sheets and practise with labs.
Instructors start at the Instructor Hub, which has syllabi, slides, kits and labs for courses.
Each component has its own license: the textbook, labs, kits and slides are non-commercial, TinyTorch is MIT, MLSys·im is Apache 2.0 and StaffML is AGPL v3.
